# chessmen

> The chessboard for the web: replay PGN games or show a FEN position on any page. One script tag, zero dependencies, no build step. Animated moves, a last-move arrow, controls, a game picker, arrows and circles, side boards for variations, 20 board themes and two Staunton piece sets. Renders SVG. Move parsing and legality come from chess.js, bundled in. By the makers of Slate Chess, the personal chess coach for Apple devices.

One script tag is enough: `dist/chessmen.all.js` holds the board, its stylesheet and the Classic Staunton pieces. Load it from a copy on your site, or from the CDN: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chessmen@0.5.0/dist/chessmen.all.js`. Each board needs a container element and a PGN (one or more games).

Minimal page:

```html
<div id="board"></div>
<script src="chessmen/dist/chessmen.all.js"></script>
<script>
  Chessmen.create(document.getElementById("board"), {
    games: '[White "Morphy"]\n[Black "Duke Karl / Count Isouard"]\n[Result "1-0"]\n\n1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 Bg4 4. dxe5 Bxf3 5. Qxf3 dxe5 6. Bc4 Nf6 7. Qb3 Qe7 8. Nc3 c6 9. Bg5 b5 10. Nxb5 cxb5 11. Bxb5+ Nbd7 12. O-O-O Rd8 13. Rxd7 Rxd7 14. Rd1 Qe6 15. Bxd7+ Nxd7 16. Qb8+ Nxb8 17. Rd8# 1-0'
  });
</script>
```

No code at all:

```html
<div data-chessmen='{"autoplay":false}'><script type="application/x-chess-pgn">1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6</script></div>
<script src="chessmen/dist/chessmen.all.js"></script>
```

Rules that avoid common mistakes:
- Moves come as PGN or SAN text ("1. e4 e5 2. Nf3"), not coordinates like "e2e4".
- A single position: `Chessmen.create(el, { fen: "<FEN>" })`. `games` also accepts a FEN string, and so does the no-code embed. A placement-only FEN means White to move.
- Several games in one string must be separated by a blank line before each `[Event` header block.
- `scheme` is one of: mahogany (default), classic, teal, green, blue, cyan, red, oak, walnut, carrara, slate, midnight, sage, mustard, terracotta, blackWhite, ember, espresso, graphite, navy.
- `pieceColours` is one of: original (default), ivoryGraphite, pearlSlate, champagneSteel, ivoryEspresso, blushBurgundy, creamCocoa, pistachioLagoon, sandClaret, porcelainNavy, parchmentMoss, amberSky. With a dark scheme (navy, graphite, espresso, ember, midnight) always use "amberSky", or black pieces disappear.
- `pieces` is "classic-staunton" (default, inside the .all.js file) or "modern-staunton", which needs one more tag after the first: `<script src="chessmen/dist/pieces/modern-staunton.js"></script>`.
- For arrows, circles and variations use `board.stage` (see the annotate example). Arrow syntax: "e2e4 green"; circle: "d7 red".
- There is no `ChessStage` global; everything is on `Chessmen` (`Chessmen.createStage` is the bare stage).

Separate files, if you'd rather choose: `dist/chessmen.css` + `dist/chessmen.js` + at least one `dist/pieces/<name>.js`. As an ES module: `import { create, registerPieceSet } from "chessmen"` and `import classic from "chessmen/pieces/classic-staunton.mjs"`, then `registerPieceSet(classic)` and add the CSS file yourself.
